summary: The manuscript reports a fully archived, preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics with retrieval disabled. The run completed as archived (N=250 pairs, one shared LLM generation per pair), the deterministic validator judged every shared candidate valid, no repairs were applied, and the paired actionable‑misconfiguration difference is exactly 0.0. The authors explicitly reconcile the preregistered RAG/poisoning intent with the executed contract (retrievals disabled) and limit conclusions accordingly. Artifacts, hashes, and the initial master prompt locator are present in the evidence bundle.
optional_revisions: Add one explicit, short sentence in Methods (if not already highlighted) making the accounting reason for model_calls_used=250 (shared single generation per pair) visually prominent so readers cannot miss why planned_episode_count=500 but model_calls_used=250.

Optionally, in Related Work briefly enumerate which cited references concretely support the RAG‑poisoning motivation vs. the validator/repair recommendation to tighten citation-to-claim alignment (this is optional because terminal bibliographic records appear sufficient).
